A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MedUnifier and provide readable methods, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, retrieval, report-generation, image-generation and ablation results in its main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative comparisons between generated and ground-truth reports.

M1.justification: The frozen ViT-g, transformer encoder, learnable embeddings, hierarchical vector quantization, latent adapters, four training objectives and PixelSNAIL generation procedure remain unchanged. Removed decoder descriptions do not establish an architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert 5x200, RSNA, SIIM-ACR and COVIDx for the same classification, retrieval and generation tasks. The new report examples do not introduce a distinct dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–5 is unchanged, including all report-generation and image-generation baselines. UniXGen in v1 and UniXGer in v3 refer to the same cited work.

E3.justification: The stated splits, preprocessing, fine-tuning proportions, zero-shot sampling, model configurations and benchmark evaluation procedures match. Dropping some higher-K ablation entries changes reported evidence without establishing a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: v3 adds two qualitative report-generation case studies in Figure 3. Existing reconstruction, objective-combination and TIG-weight analyses remain; the classification ablations added to main Table 6 already appeared in v1's appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 5 changes MedUnifier's FID from 42.6 to 46.2 under the same stated evaluation setup, without explaining the update. Tables 1–4 retain their scores; v3 adds report examples and omits some objective-combination mAP@5 and mAP@10 results previously in Table 6.

T1.justification: Equations 1–24 retain the same formulation and objectives. Shortened dimensional explanations and bottom-to-bot notation changes do not alter the mathematics; neither version adds theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims of a unified medical VLP framework, benefits from discrete visual generation, strong downstream performance and potential for out-of-distribution augmentation. Consolidating contribution bullets does not change their substantive scope.

C2.justification: The new Figure 3 interprets generated reports as showing strong semantic alignment and highlights matching findings. It does not discuss the example's disagreement about chest-tube removal. Existing mechanism explanations and applicability claims otherwise remain.

D1.justification: v1's Appendix 2 specifies one top deconvolution block, its transposed convolution, ReLU and batch normalization, and four bottom decoder blocks. These details disappear from v3's corresponding Section 8; other principal hyperparameters, preprocessing and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 removes the image-space versus latent-space diffusion discussion and associated references, including eDiff-I, cascaded diffusion and latent diffusion. The central positioning relative to existing medical VLP and generative approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 condenses passages throughout the introduction, related work, method and conclusion, consolidates contribution bullets and updates author information. The section sequence and overall narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, adds the report-comparison figure, and moves the original generation Figure 3 to supplementary Figure 6. Table 5 becomes two side-by-side groups, while Table 6 combines retrieval with previously supplementary classification ablations.

improvement.justification: The report examples and more visible classification ablations aid inspection, but v3 removes decoder construction details useful for reproducing the image generator. Its new Figure 3 also emphasizes semantic agreement without acknowledging the contradiction about chest-tube removal. These limited losses in reproducibility and balanced interpretation outweigh the modest presentation gains.
